newsitem.title: UK: Nationwide urges vote against converters.
newsitem.headline: Nationwide urges vote against converters.

text.p: Britain's Nationwide Building Society on Wednesday urged its members to vote against a group which wants it to ditch its mutual status and follow others in a rush for a stock market flotation.

The group, called "Members for Conversion" is fielding five candidates for election to the Nationwide's board. The postal vote for the re-election of the five executives begins in mid-June and must be completed within a month.

Members for Conversion wants the Nationwide to follow others such as the Alliance & Leicester, the Halifax, Northern Rock and the Woolwich in voting for a stock exchange flotation and becoming a bank, with a share windfall for members.

Nationwide chief executive Brian Davis told a press briefing that the board was asking its savers and borrowers, the society's members, to vote for the existing board members seeking re-election and not to be taken in by the short-term windfall offered by those seeking conversion.
Of the Nationwide's 3.5 million members, only 290,000 voted at the last election of board members, and Davis said a good turnout was important this time round.

"We would like people to vote," he said. While he disagreed with the 1,000 pound figure suggested by the group as the amount that would be freed up to the average member, he said he could not comment on what the likely realisation could be.
Davis re-iterated the view that mutual building societies will offer savers and borrowers better rates than banks or societies that are converting to bank status.

"You have got to bear in mind that mortgages last quite a long time and savings are over a long period," Davis said, pointing out that the benefits of mutuality were far longer-term than a one-off windfall.

While the advocates of conversion are not expected to find their way onto the board, Nationwide is taking them seriously and if they do get good support, the Nationwide will look at the results and will hold a board meeting regardless.
